questions.stem: Which of the following is a fundamental physical quantity?
questions.explanation: Time is one of the seven fundamental SI quantities; it is defined independently and its unit, the second, is a base unit. Force, density and pressure all have units built from base units, so they are derived quantities.

distractorRationale.a: Force is derived: 1 N = 1 kg m s⁻², which combines mass, length and time
distractorRationale.b: Density is mass ÷ volume, so its unit kg m⁻³ combines two base units
distractorRationale.d: Pressure is force ÷ area, giving kg m⁻¹ s⁻²

questions.stem: The SI unit of thermodynamic temperature is the
questions.explanation: The kelvin is the SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature, measured from absolute zero. The Celsius degree is the same size as a kelvin but its zero is shifted to the ice point, so it is a practical scale rather than the SI base unit.

distractorRationale.a: The Celsius scale is widely used but is not the SI base unit because its zero is not absolute zero
distractorRationale.c: Fahrenheit is not an SI unit at all
distractorRationale.d: The joule measures energy, not temperature; heat and temperature are different quantities

questions.stem: The mole is one of the seven fundamental SI quantities.
questions.explanation: True. Amount of substance is a fundamental quantity and its SI unit is the mole (mol). The full list of seven is length, mass, time, electric current, thermodynamic temperature, amount of substance and luminous intensity.

questions.stem: Expressed in fundamental SI units, the newton is equivalent to
questions.explanation: From Newton's second law, $F = ma$. Mass has unit kg and acceleration has unit $\text{m}\,\text{s}^{-2}$, so $1\ \text{N} = 1\ \text{kg}\,\text{m}\,\text{s}^{-2}$.

distractorRationale.a: This is the unit of momentum, $mv$, which uses velocity rather than acceleration
distractorRationale.c: This is the joule, obtained by multiplying the newton by a further metre
distractorRationale.d: This is the pascal, obtained by dividing the newton by an area

questions.stem: Which of the following is the unit of pressure expressed in fundamental SI units?
questions.explanation: Pressure is force per unit area, so its unit is $\text{kg}\,\text{m}\,\text{s}^{-2} \div \text{m}^{2}$. One metre cancels, leaving $\text{kg}\,\text{m}^{-1}\,\text{s}^{-2}$, which is the pascal.

distractorRationale.b: This is the newton — the force itself, with no division by area
distractorRationale.c: Obtained by dividing by m² but forgetting that force already contains one metre
distractorRationale.d: This is the watt, the unit of power

questions.stem: The SI unit of density is
questions.explanation: Density is mass per unit volume, so the SI unit is kilogram divided by cubic metre, written $\text{kg}\,\text{m}^{-3}$. Dividing means the exponent of the metre is negative.

distractorRationale.a: A common laboratory unit, but grams and centimetres are not SI base units
distractorRationale.b: Uses area instead of volume — this is the unit of mass per unit area
distractorRationale.d: Multiplies by volume instead of dividing, so the exponent sign is wrong

questions.stem: Which pair consists of two derived quantities only?
questions.explanation: Weight is a force ($W = mg$, unit $\text{kg}\,\text{m}\,\text{s}^{-2}$) and density is mass per unit volume (unit $\text{kg}\,\text{m}^{-3}$). Both are combinations of base quantities, so both are derived.

distractorRationale.a: Both mass and time are fundamental quantities
distractorRationale.c: Both length and electric current are fundamental quantities
distractorRationale.d: Volume is derived, but thermodynamic temperature is fundamental, so only one of the pair qualifies

questions.stem: A solid cube has each side of length 20 cm. Calculate its volume. Give your answer in cubic metres.
questions.explanation: First convert to metres: $20\ \text{cm} = 0.20\ \text{m}$. Then $V = l^3 = (0.20)^3 = 0.008\ \text{m}^3$. Note that you must cube the converted length, not the value in centimetres.

questions.stem: A torch bulb draws a current of 250 mA. Express this current in amperes. Give your answer in amperes.
questions.explanation: The prefix milli means $10^{-3}$, so $250\ \text{mA} = 250 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{A} = 0.25\ \text{A}$. Always convert to amperes before substituting into $V = IR$ or $P = IV$.

questions.stem: A physical quantity has the unit $\text{kg}\,\text{m}^{2}\,\text{s}^{-3}\,\text{A}^{-1}$. The quantity is
questions.explanation: Potential difference is energy per unit charge: $V = \frac{W}{Q}$. Energy has unit $\text{kg}\,\text{m}^{2}\,\text{s}^{-2}$ and charge has unit $\text{A}\,\text{s}$, so $[V] = \frac{\text{kg}\,\text{m}^{2}\,\text{s}^{-2}}{\text{A}\,\text{s}} = \text{kg}\,\text{m}^{2}\,\text{s}^{-3}\,\text{A}^{-1}$, which is the volt.

distractorRationale.a: Charge has unit A s, with no mass or length in it at all
distractorRationale.b: Power is $\text{kg}\,\text{m}^{2}\,\text{s}^{-3}$ — the same but without the $\text{A}^{-1}$
distractorRationale.d: Resistance is $\frac{V}{I}$, giving $\text{kg}\,\text{m}^{2}\,\text{s}^{-3}\,\text{A}^{-2}$, so the current exponent would be −2

questions.stem: A rectangular metal block measures 5.0 cm by 4.0 cm by 2.0 cm and has a mass of 240 g. Calculate its density. Give your answer in kilograms per cubic metre.
questions.explanation: Volume $= 5.0 \times 4.0 \times 2.0 = 40\ \text{cm}^3$. Since $1\ \text{cm}^3 = 10^{-6}\ \text{m}^3$, the volume is $4.0 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{m}^3$. Mass $= 240\ \text{g} = 0.240\ \text{kg}$. Density $= \frac{0.240}{4.0 \times 10^{-5}} = 6000\ \text{kg}\,\text{m}^{-3}$.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a base SI quantity?
questions.explanation: Volume is a derived quantity, not a base SI quantity. The base SI quantities include length, mass, time, electric current, thermodynamic temperature, amount of substance, and luminous intensity.

distractorRationale.a: Length is a base SI quantity.
distractorRationale.b: Mass is a base SI quantity.
distractorRationale.d: Time is a base SI quantity.

questions.explanation: The derived SI unit of force is the Newton, which is defined as the force required to accelerate a mass of one kilogram at a rate of one meter per second squared.

distractorRationale.a: Joule is the unit of energy.
distractorRationale.c: Watt is the unit of power.
distractorRationale.d: Pascal is the unit of pressure.

questions.stem: If a derived unit is expressed as $	ext{kg}	ext{m}^{2}	ext{s}^{-2}$, what physical quantity does it represent?
questions.explanation: The unit $	ext{kg}	ext{m}^{2}	ext{s}^{-2}$ represents energy, specifically the Joule, which is the work done when a force of one newton moves an object one meter.

distractorRationale.c: Giga- represents one billion.
distractorRationale.d: Tera- represents one trillion.

distractorRationale.c: Pound is a unit of mass in the imperial system.

questions.explanation: To convert kilograms to grams, you multiply by 1000. Therefore, 2.5 kg is equal to 2.5 × 1000 g, which equals 2500 g.

distractorRationale.c: 25 g is incorrect; it is a much smaller quantity.

distractorRationale.c: kg·m/s² is the unit of force, not energy.
distractorRationale.d: kg·m²/s is incorrect; it does not represent energy.
